summary: A 1977 standard for the format of ARPA network text messages. It replaced RFC 724 and was itself replaced by RFC 822.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 733 defines a common format for ARPA Network text messages. It separates structured header fields from the message body and specifies how programs can parse them.

questions: what was the standard email format on arpanet
how does rfc 733 structure a text message
subtitle: Defines a structured header and body format for text messages on the ARPA Network.

tldr.problem: ARPA Network mail systems needed a shared format for message headers and addresses.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 733 defines fields such as Date, From, To and Subject, with syntax for addresses, folded headers, dates and message bodies.
tldr.outcome: It replaced earlier message formats and was itself obsoleted by RFC 822.

today: RFC 733 was obsoleted by RFC 822. RFC 733 is a historical specification for ARPA Network text messages.

sections.title: A Common Text Message Format
sections.content:
RFC 733 specifies syntax for text messages passed between computer users as electronic mail. It revises earlier ARPANET mail specifications and separates a general framework, formal syntax, semantics and examples.

The specification defines what hosts pass between them. It does not require systems to support particular features or prescribe user interfaces.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC sets shared rules for ARPA Network text messages. It defines message structure, not the design of mail programs.

sections.title: Headers and Message Body
sections.content:
A message has a rigidly formatted header followed by a body of text. A null line separates the headers from the body. Header fields use a field name, a colon and a field body; some fields have an internal structure, while fields such as Subject are treated as text.

Headers may be folded across lines when a continuation line begins with whitespace. The RFC also allows user-defined fields within its field-delimiting rules.
sections.plainLanguage: The header contains labeled fields, followed by a blank line and the message text. Long header fields can continue on an indented line.

sections.title: Address and Reference Fields
sections.content:
The RFC defines address forms for individual mailboxes, lists, groups, included address lists and postal addresses. It distinguishes the author in From, the sending agent in Sender and suggested reply destinations in Reply-To.

It also defines Message-ID, In-Reply-To, References and Keywords fields. The Bcc field identifies additional recipients, and its contents are not included in copies sent to primary and secondary recipients.
sections.plainLanguage: Address fields identify authors, senders, recipients and reply destinations. Other fields identify a message or the messages it refers to.
